The First Case: Deshan’s Address to the Assembly,
as selected by Chan Master Xuedou Mingjue from the "Striking the Joint" collection of Chan Master Guo Yuanwu.
Deshan addressed the assembly, saying, "Tonight I shall not answer questions. (These words still ring in our ears. Anyone who asks a question shall receive thirty blows.

(He struck them, saying, "Eat these blows! At that time, a monk came forward and bowed. Deshan immediately struck him. (A man who forgets what precedes and loses track of what follows. The monk said, "I have not even asked a question yet.
(This is actually quite remarkable. Deshan asked, "Where are you from? (He changed the monk's very eyes. The monk replied, "Silla."
[The Master] said, "A person! (Yet he changes Deshan’s eyes. Deshan said, "Before you have even stepped onto the boat's railing, thirty blows of the staff would be well-deserved.
(How great and small Deshan is, making such a move! Fayan picked up [the case] and said, "Great and small Deshan, you turn a single story into two pieces.

(A lacquer bucket shines light at night. Yuanying picked up [the case] and said, "Great and small Deshan, a dragon’s head and a snake’s tail. (A tortoise drills through a wall. Xuedou picked up [the case] and said, "The two old masters..."

Although one may skillfully trim the long to supplement the short and set aside the heavy to follow the light—(the phrase "錯下名言" [mistakenly applying names and words] follows below)—even so, it is still not permissible to claim one has seen Deshan.
(Have you ever dreamed of Deshan? Why? Because Deshan was much like one who wields authority beyond the borders;

he possessed a sword that, when it was time to sever, would not hesitate to do so—a blade that does not invite chaos. (Dangerous! Do you all wish to recognize this monk from Silla? (Is it not you, the *jiaoli* [Dharma teacher]? It is simply...
"This is a blind man bumping into a pillar—take him out yourself.

The Master said, "The ancients brought up every single instance and every single scene to clarify this very matter. Furthermore, before the World-Honored One even raised the flower, what was the underlying principle?
That is why it is said later that 'buying a hat to fit the head' and 'beating the rhythm according to the seating arrangement.'"

Now, if you merely focus on memorizing myriad details and entangle yourself in conceptual knots, when will there ever be an end? To possess much knowledge and many explanations only serves to increase affliction.
When an ancient master cites or comments upon a single precedent or kōan, one must first be able to penetrate the intent of that ancient; only then may one pick it up and present it.
Take, for instance, Deshan: he was originally from Western Sichuan and lectured on the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*.
The Abbot heard that the Chan school was flourishing greatly in the south. He remarked, "In the south, such a proliferation of demonic offspring!

Thereupon, he ceased his lectures and dismissed his disciples, intending to take his commentaries and sub-commentaries to destroy the Chan school. However, upon reaching Longtan, he attained great enlightenment under the Master’s words.
Later, while residing at Deshan, he would search the halls once every three days; whenever he saw any written texts, he would immediately burn them. Twelve hours [of the day].
He was struck by the winds and rains of the Middle Way. Later, he emerged from the cliffs of Yantou and Xuefeng, appearing like a dragon or a tiger.
When it came to his striking of conceptual entanglements, he possessed a truly extraordinary quality. One day he addressed the assembly, saying: "You need only leave the mind free of affairs."
When the mind is free from objects, it is empty yet spiritual, still yet wondrous. Furthermore, it is said that to grasp at emptiness or pursue echoes is to weary your mind and spirit;
it is like awakening from a dream to find it was not real, yet even this awakening is not itself an awakening. One day, Yantou came to attend upon Deshan.

As soon as he spread out his sitting mat, Deshan struck him with his staff and shoved him down the steps. Yantou descended the steps, picked up his mat, and went straight to the meditation hall. The next day...
He went up to pay his respects and stood in attendance. Mount said, "Where did you learn this kind of hypocrisy?
Yantou replied, "I do not dare deceive myself. Mount said, "In the future, you will defecate upon my head!
Now, tell me, what did he see that he did not strike him? Is this not a most extraordinary matter?
Only then can it be so. One day Yantou came to attend upon Deshan; as soon as his foot crossed the threshold, he asked, "Is this ordinary or is it sacred?
Deshan gave a shout, and Yantou immediately prostrated himself. But tell me, what did this father and son see that they were so extraordinary?
The former master Wuzu said, "Since he has already opened a shop, why does he not..."
[The Master] gave a response. "Furthermore, where does Dàodéshān’s intention lie? This monk was truly extraordinary; leaping out from among the assembly, he immediately prostrated himself.
Dàodéshān struck him—just like a hawk seizing a swallow or a falcon catching a pigeon. As Fǎyǎn remarked when citing this story, "How great [is Dàodéshān]!
He split the discourse into two parts; it could be said that he settled the case according to the facts. Yuánmíng...
I pick up the path. Great Master Deshan—dragon’s head and snake’s tail—is merely fitting a wedge into a hole. How do you understand this public case now?
If you understand it as two separate parts, you will have no connection to it. Even if you understand it as a dragon’s head and a snake’s tail, you still have no connection to it.
Since you do not understand it in either of these ways, how do you understand it ultimately? Tell me, what about the second...?
"Old Master! Why do you handle this case in such a way? Everyone, try to look at it with your own eyes. An ancient said:
'When a lion bites a man, mad dogs chase after clods of earth. How can you see through Deshan now?

That is why I have selected ten ancient cases and handled them in ten different ways; you must go beyond the original intent of those ancients before you can truly call it 'handling an ancient case' (niangu). It is just like..."

Master Fu said: "Night after night one embraces the Buddha in sleep; morning after morning one rises together with him. If you wish to know where the Buddha goes, it is simply this very sound of speech.
Look at how Xuansha commented on this: "How great Master Fu is! He merely recognizes that which is bright and alert.
Furthermore, when Lingyun saw peach blossoms, he attained awakening and said: "Ever since the first sight of the peach blossoms..."
Now there is no further doubt. Xuansha said, "It is accurate, most accurate; yet I dare guarantee that you, elder brother, have not yet reached the ultimate.
But tell me, where does his meaning lie? Xuedou is just like the ancients; first he takes up the words of those two elders and says:
"Although these two venerable masters were skilled at cutting the long to patch the short and discarding the heavy to follow the light, tell me, where [does the meaning lie]?"
This is a place for cutting the long to supplement the short. What place is it where one abandons the heavy to follow the light?
These two points clearly examine Deshan. Why did Xuedou, having brought them forth, nevertheless say, "If you wish to see Deshan, you have not yet attained it"?
Xuedou’s subsequent remark, “It is difficult even for Deshan to see this much,” was intended to reveal this very point. Later people gave a distorted interpretation, saying:
"Fayan’s perfect clarity was merely cutting the long to patch the short and abandoning the heavy to follow the light;
he did nothing but issue proclamations—what connection has that to the truth? Xuedou takes up the matter and asks: "What is Deshan like? He is like a general beyond the passes."
The military is like this: possessing both majesty and authority, it has a sword for others. When one ought to strike but does not, one does not invite chaos.
Xuedou’s presentation of this case is such that there are not a few who misunderstand it. Xuedou has already presented it above.
